1.why: All /api/mfa/* routes call requireSession(request, true) and derive the account solely from the server-side session map keyed by the HttpOnly cookie, so no user identifier is accepted from the client (no IDOR).

2.why: The identity confirmation code is generated per session (session.identityCode) and TOTP is derived from a per-account secret, so a code valid for one user cannot verify another user.

3.why: Nothing in enrol/verify iterates or deletes other sessions for the account, and the session id is not regenerated when MFA is enabled, so any pre-existing session remains valid (subject only to idle/absolute timeouts).

4.why: OTP secrets are stored only as AES-GCM ciphertext via encryptAtRest, and recovery codes are stored solely as SHA-256 hashes in account.recoveryHashes.

5.why: All secrets, session ids, CSRF tokens, 6-digit codes and recovery codes come from crypto.getRandomValues (bytes()/randomToken/randomSixDigitCode), a CSPRNG, with only minor modulo bias.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used and the only cookie is bank_session with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict, though secrets/codes do live transiently in JS memory and the on-page log panel.

7.why: Server-side validators validEmail, validPhone, validOtp and normalizeRecovery strictly whitelist formats before use, and there is no SQL/string-concatenated data store at all.

8.why: Dynamic values (manualSecret, provisioningUri, recovery codes, log entries) are inserted with textContent/createElement, innerHTML is only used with static markup, and the CSP is nonce-based with object-src 'none'.

9.why: The application issues no redirects whatsoever (no Location headers or client navigation), so there is no open-redirect surface, but equally no explicit allow-list implementation exists.

10.why: baseHeaders sets a strict nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store on every response.

11.why: sessionCookie() emits `bank_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=...` and the clearing cookie uses the same attributes.

12.why: Although errors are generic and stack-trace free, the API deliberately returns mockIdentityCode, manualSecret, provisioningUri, mockAuthenticatorOtp and plaintext recoveryCodes, which the client then console.log()s and renders into a visible Logs panel.

13.why: The identity code has issuedAt/expiresAt (5 min) plus a consumed flag, and enrolment TOTP is accepted only for the current 30-second period which is then recorded in usedOtpPeriods to prevent replay.

14.why: Sign-in uses a hashed limiter key with 5 failures then a 10-minute lock, and identity, enrolment OTP and recovery redemption each track failures and set lockedUntil for LOCKOUT_MS.

15.why: A fresh session id is minted at sign-in, idle (20 min) and absolute (8 h) timeouts are enforced, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie, but the id is not rotated when the second-factor/identity verification elevates the session.
